svg.title: TOPAK B3 — Changing the floor: the route is computed, every solver holds carries a checked proof, and the floor in force was built in three gated stages
svg.desc: A candidate floor F′ is compared with the deployed floor F in both directions; the answer, not the author, picks the authority path. A Build author is Byzantine by premise and cannot relabel a relaxation as a tightening; a wrong solver could, until ADR-0030 A1 made the solver trusted for nothing. The same gate run checks the three floor gates. The floor in force is the proposed floor's emergency stage, built from the genesis draft through labels and control, each stage gated; it is genesis-provisional: gated, pinned and enforced, and ratified only when the bootstrap reviewer establishes that it is fit (ADR-0030 A3).

text.tspan: Does it change the rules floor?

svg.text: The rules floor bounds issuances, not admits, and stays mechanism-checked (ADR-0030 §7).

text.tspan: Rules floor: two keys, both directions

svg.text: Any change, tighter or looser: an anchor issuance and a promotion
Tightening needs both too: a tighter rules floor constrains the anchor,
cedar symcc, Cedar's symbolic compiler, encodes both floors over schema S into SMT queries; the encoding is sound by proof (ADR-0030 §3). A holds is an UNSAT from the solver, so it
passes the proof-carrying gate (right) before it counts.
The analysis results join the gate-evidence digest that every promotion vote binds to (ADR-0024 §3).
Every counted grant seat grants; votes bind to (artifact, gate
Tightening the policy floor is not a rules change (ADR-0025 §1).
Relaxing the policy floor, or adding an exception, is a rules
change. Incomparable goes the expensive way by default.
It removes a reviewer's assertion from the one spot where Build principals
choose the authority path for their own change (ADR-0030 §5).
Every envelope and carve-out stated in the floor is floor text, recusal (B7)
included: relaxing one is a floor relaxation, routed here (ADR-0030 §10

text.tspan: The proof-carrying gate (ADR-0030 §5 with A1; G7 §2.8)

svg.text: Runs the analysis; reads only the verdict from the solver path it is given, so a wrapper needs no change to cedar. cedar-policy-cli 4.13.0.
Keeps every query; runs cvc5 with proof production on; discards the solver's restatement of the query; prefixes the proof with declarations derived from the query's own
text; requires every assumption in the proof to be one of the query's assertions verbatim; refuses a restatement that disagrees. sha256 dfe159e9c21a549e.
The solver: trusted for nothing. Proof format: cvc5's Cooperating Proof Calculus (CPC); Alethe was tried and refused for the queries' set theory. Binary
Checks the proof of false against the CPC signature vendored unchanged from cvc5 1.4.0 (tools/cpc/, tree 6d7e8d208d223985; binary 4eb41c1f1f9fce88).
Independent in code, not in authorship. Trust root T-0045-14.
→ holds✓: the query's declarations and assertions entail false; the query,
proof and verdict digests join the gate evidence.
→ cedar reports an analysis failure, never a holds. Fails closed.
It routes a change to more consent or fails a gate, so a wrong one can only subtract (ADR-0030 §5).

text.tspan: : what the checker does not reach

svg.text: cedar decides some analyses with no solver query at all, by folding the authorizer term: every never-errors check on the floor, and a permit-all under always-allows. They rest
on the Cedar engine's row, T-0045-3, not on a proof: 25 of 29 holds in the genesis run of 2026.10.01 (G7 §3, result 4; item 69, as at G9), 41 of 56 in the run of the floor in
The checker certifies that the query entails false, not that cedar's encoding of the floor is faithful; that is T-0045-3 and ADR-0030 §3's soundness argument. The
signature's rules are trusted as cvc5's authors wrote them.
ADR-0053, B36: the genesis floor's 23 totality rows, and since R3 the floor in force's 41, are proved in Lean under cedar-spec v4.13.0's model, by its proved validator
soundness (floor/lean; H7). They would then rest on the Lean kernel (T-0045-37) and on T-0045-3's own premise, the engine's fidelity to that model, and no longer on
cedar's folding code. The labels and control stages are not stated in Lean; the reference links neither.
Declared by a deployment that runs the gates without the checker, and the position of every gate run before 2026.10.01: a wrong holds lets a relaxation reach a promotion
Subtractive mitigation: make every floor change two-key, tightening included (ADR-0030 §8).
The checker is pinned by three digests in the gate header; no mechanism release exists to carry them (T-0045-30; item 68, as at G9). Gate evidence is now recorded by an
operator's signed AttestGates: attributed, and still an assertion (ADR-0024 A3; G10 item 57).

text.tspan: Since Batch 34: what S and a bundle's load gain (ADR-0030 A2)

svg.text: S gains what the label forbids read: clearSet and inputLabels in Run's context; on the tool, whether it is outward and which destination inputs are literals or labelled
handles. The mechanism computes them; history enters S only as named attributes a mechanism release adds.
A bundle whose allowlist data fails ADR-0049 §6's W1 to W10 does not load, a mechanism constant checked after the signature. W7 and W8 read the two lists the
issued rules carry (ADR-0025 A2): adding to either is an issuance, routed like any rules change.

text.tspan: The floor in force is genesis-provisional (ADR-0030 A3)

svg.text: Not ratified by any batch; ratified when the bootstrap reviewer establishes that it is fit (ADR-0029 §5, step 6). That gives floor fitness an owner and a time, and no test
Routing still applies to it: a change is classified against it, and removing X1 was a tightening, a floor change with the gates run (ADR-0052 §9).

text.tspan: The three floor gates (ADR-0007, decidable on the floor since ADR-0030 §5)

svg.text: Validation against S, and never-errors over the whole floor, per policy per action it covers.
Any evaluation error is a deny, so an erroring forbid cannot be skipped into an allow.
Not always-allows: the floor refuses some conforming request, per action.
A floor that permits everything admits every bundle and discharges every property over nothing: the widest silent failure in the system (ToO
Non-vacuity and not always-denies: the floor both admits and refuses, per action.
An action class the floor always denies is declared as such, never left implicit.

A failing check returns a counterexample request. The gate run adds every entry matters (the floor minus any one policy is not equivalent to it), routing controls and negative controls. Three gates are not enough: a fourth, floor fitness, is owned and timed since Batch 34 and has no test: the bootstrap reviewer establishes it, and with that the floor is ratified (ADR-0029 A4; ADR-0030 A3; G10 items 2, 87). The gates say the text is well-formed, non-vacuous and
minimal, not that it is the right floor.

The table of floor/proposed/README.md, in full. The genesis floor has 17 policies and 62 cases. Each stage passes the genesis gates as they stand, plus routing candidates for its new entries (four for labels, nine by control, eleven by emergency); no holds in any run is without a checked proof. A
rerun reproduces each results file byte for byte (G10 §3).

text.tspan: What the stages do not show

svg.text: The admit-time half only: ADR-0047's F4 to F6 are load checks on bundle data (W7 to W9), made by the mechanism, not Cedar.
The floor trusts its inputs: clearSet, peerLive and the rest are facts the lift supplies; Labels.tla and Operators.tla model them. The floor's decision on an operator's
request is not in the trace model (G10 §3).
The stage files open with a wrong comment, "not what the reference follows"; the bytes are kept as gated so cited digests stay pinned. Correcting it is a gate rerun and new
